transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Marco Reyes (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (NimbleEdge Head of ML), Evan Cho (Platform), Lena Ruiz (Security), Raj Malhotra (Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery to validate integration approach for NimbleEdge's LLM features. Main concerns: latency targets, quota/rate-limit semantics across gateway/proxy, SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost), and private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Redwood team to share pricing/POC plan and SDK examples; customer to share workload samples.

Topics covered:
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Proxy/gateway architecture: sidecar vs central proxy, auth, rate-limits/quotas
- SDKs and first-class support for LangChain + LlamaIndex connectors
- Observability: logs, traces, per-route token cost, and metrics hooks
- Caching and batching (K-V cache, prefix caching) to reduce cost
- Security: KMS integration, SSO, SOC 2, audit logs

Action items (captured quickly at meeting): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros from our side, I'm Sofia, technical AE, with Daniel our solutions engineer and Marco on post-sales.
[00:00:15] Priya (NimbleEdge): Hi, I'm Priya, lead ML. Evan is our platform lead, and Lena handles security. We just want to make sure the integration path is clear before we commit to a pilot.
[00:00:32] Daniel (Redwood SE): Great. Today we want to understand your topology, what you call latency SLOs, and how you'd prefer to surface rate-limits and quotas to your apps.
[00:00:45] Evan (NimbleEdge): High level: we have a microservices platform on k8s, some workloads are latency sensitive — p50 around 100ms for small prompts, p95 under 350ms. We also need to throttle per-team quotas and global QPS caps.
[00:01:10] Raj (NimbleEdge Infra): Also curious about hosting modes. We may start with Redwood Hosted but likely shift to Dedicated or Private VPC in Q3 depending on cost and compliance.
[00:01:28] Sofia: Makes sense. Quick mapping: Hosted = fastest to get started, usage-based. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost. Private = customer-managed VPC or on-prem with KMS control. There are tradeoffs on TTF (time to first token) and management overhead.
[00:01:50] Lena (Security): On Private, what exactly sits in our VPC? Is the control plane still Redwood-managed? How are keys handled?
[00:02:05] Marco (Redwood CSM): Private can be configured with a private control plane + customer-managed networking. Keys can be integrated with your KMS/HSM; audit logs forward to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC 2 docs in the follow-up.
[00:02:20] Priya: For the integration part: our data scientists use LangChain and some in-house LlamaIndex connectors. Does Redwood have first-class SDKs or ready-made connectors?
[00:02:37] Daniel: Yes — our SDKs include helper adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns. We have example repos: one for LangChain chains and another for LlamaIndex index builders. They handle streaming, function-calls-ish patterns, and manage KV cache hints. We'll post a link to the example repo.
[00:02:55] Priya: Nice. Two questions — how do you recommend we place Redwood calls in our stack? Direct from app to Redwood, or through an internal gateway/proxy?
[00:03:12] Evan: We usually put a lightweight internal proxy in front so we can enforce per-team quotas, add tracing headers, and rewrite prompts.
[00:03:25] Daniel: That's a common pattern. We support both approaches. If you use a gateway, you can run Redwood client in the gateway or call Redwood directly from services and have the gateway only for auth and quotas. Each has implications for batching and KV cache locality.
[00:03:44] Raj: Could you expand on KV cache locality? We're worried about losing cache hit-rate if calls are sharded across pods.
[00:03:57] Daniel: Right. Our runtime supports prefix KV caching and we recommend colocating cache with the serving pool that holds the KV shards. For microservices behind a gateway, consult caching patterns — sidecar + sticky routing keeps the KV warm. If you use a central proxy that fans out, you'll see lower cache efficiency unless you pin requests by user/session.
[00:04:22] Priya: So for embeddings-heavy flows (RAG), would Dedicated give us better cache hit rates?
[00:04:32] Daniel: Dedicated gives you more control over which GPUs and serving pools handle your requests, so you can co-locate the embedding store and improve locality. Hosted tries to maximize utilization across tenants and may evict KV sooner.
[00:04:48] Lena: On quotas — we need per-team monthly token quotas plus burst QPS limits. Can Redwood enforce both?
[00:04:59] Sofia: Yes. We have rate-limit primitives at route and token level. Policies can be enforced at the edge (gateway) or in the control plane with enforcement at the serving layer. For Dedicated/Private, you get extra policy knobs: per-consumer, per-route, burst windows.
[00:05:20] Evan: Is there an SDK hook we can use to emit traces and token counts into our tracing system? We use Jaeger and Datadog.
[00:05:29] Daniel: We export OpenTelemetry spans and emit per-request metrics including token usage, latency, and which model/version served. You can connect to Datadog agent or forward OTLP to Jaeger. We also have a lightweight middleware for the SDK to add trace-context headers.
[00:05:47] Priya: Great — does the SDK automatically split tokens to avoid hitting per-request maxs? We've had issues with chunking.
[00:05:58] Daniel: The SDK has utilities for streaming and automatic chunking for long contexts; for embeddings we recommend batching at the client with our batch helper functions. There are knobs to control max_tokens per call and the SDK will raise a specific error code you can catch.
[00:06:15] Raj: Trying to understand the proxy options. If we run a central proxy, can Redwood's auth be token-based with short-lived tokens so we can rotate at the proxy?
[00:06:28] Sofia: Yes short-lived tokens and mutual TLS are supported. For Private, we can integrate with your IdP for SAML/SSO for the control plane and issue scoped API creds for the proxy.
[00:06:40] Lena: On compliance: SOC 2 and data residency — does Hosted store logs or payloads externally? We have legal constraints around PII retention.
[00:06:52] Marco: Hosted keeps logs for a configurable retention period — by default it's 30 days. For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated with log forwarding to your SIEM or Private where logs never leave your VPC. We'll attach the retention and deletion policy doc.
[00:07:08] Priya: Back to observability: can we get per-model, per-route cost breakdown for chargeback? That is, tokens billed per-team.
[00:07:18] Daniel: Yes — our Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns. You can also push token-level metrics to your Prometheus instance and build chargeback dashboards.
[00:07:30] Evan: Example: we want monthly chargebacks by team and feature flag — do you support tags or metadata on calls?
[00:07:38] Sofia: Calls can include metadata tags; they show up in billing and in traces. We'll include an example of the tag header format.
[00:07:50] Priya: What about model fallbacks? If a high-cost model is unavailable, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[00:07:58] Daniel: Yes — routing policies can prefer certain models and have fallbacks. We have automatic fallback to compatible variants and can route by latency/cost goals. In Dedicated you get more control over model variants and pinning.
[00:08:12] Raj: Any cold-start latency concerns for function-calling or streaming? We've had spikes when kernels load.
[00:08:22] Daniel: Cold-starts are real — kernel and kernel selection, and KV warmup. We mitigate with warm pools and pre-warming hooks; Dedicated reduces the chance since capacity is reserved. You can also configure a keep-warm traffic pattern.
[00:08:35] Priya: We're assessing pilot success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 400ms on our small prompts in the pilot, 2) model quality parity with our baseline, 3) <15% unit cost increase versus our current infra. Any concerns?
[00:08:52] Sofia: Those are reasonable. We'll run a scoped benchmark, and if Dedicated is chosen we can simulate production concurrency to prove cost and latency.
[00:09:05] Lena: On the technical deep-dive later — I'd like specifics of audit logs, key wrapping, and HSM options.
[00:09:14] Marco: Noted; we'll have the security team run a call or send detailed docs.
[00:09:22] Speaker 6 (mislabelled): Quick aside, do you support per-route transformation?
[00:09:30] Daniel: Yes — the gateway can rewrite prompts, mask pii, enrich with context, or add agent orchestration. We provide middleware plugins in the SDK and examples for LangChain agents.
[00:09:48] Priya: Could you show us a quick snippet of how LangChain would call Redwood?
[00:09:55] Daniel: Sure, high level: import the redwood sdk, instantiate with tracer and auth, use the LangChain adapter to wrap the LLM class. Example: redwood.Client(...); from redwood.adapters.langchain import RedwoodLLM; llm = RedwoodLLM(client, model='redwood-2-medium'); then you can pass into chains. We'll share the repo link after.
[00:10:20] Priya: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We rely on embeddings + index builders heavily.
[00:10:26] Daniel: LlamaIndex is supported; the adapter handles streaming embeddings and batching. Note that large embedding batches get better throughput but you'll want to tune memory for the batched calls. We'll include recommended batch sizes per GPU type.
[00:10:40] Evan: About quotas enforcement — if we put quota logic at the proxy, does Redwood double-charge tokens if the proxy retries?
[00:10:50] Sofia: Billing is token-usage based at service level. Retries will increase token usage if they re-send prompts. We recommend idempotency keys and client-side dedupe. We also expose middleware to detect duplicate requests.
[00:11:05] Raj: Let's talk scale: if we hit spikes of 600 QPS for short bursts, what's the best path?
[00:11:14] Daniel: For bursts, Dedicated with burst capacity or Hosted with autoscaling works. For consistent high QPS, Dedicated gives predictable throughput. The gateway can smooth bursts; we also recommend request hedging for small prompts to reduce tail latency.
[00:11:30] Priya: Any limitations on streaming and function calling when behind a proxy?
[00:11:38] Daniel: Streaming works through proxies that support websockets or HTTP/2. If you're doing server-sent events through a proxy, verify connection timeout settings. Function-calling is a structured output, it's fine through proxies but ensure the proxy doesn't drop large JSON bodies.
[00:11:55] Lena: How are error codes surfaced? We need consistent status codes for our orchestration layers.
[00:12:02] Daniel: We return standard HTTP codes plus a structured error payload with a Redwood error code field. The SDK maps these to exceptions. We'll share the error-code matrix.
[00:12:14] Priya: Can we play a short end-to-end flow? Maybe a simple RAG query and demonstrate token counting?
[00:12:22] Sofia: We didn't plan a live demo today but we can do a short scripted example — Daniel, want to narrate?
[00:12:28] Daniel: Sure — imagine a user question, we call embeddings endpoint in batch, call the reranker, then generation. Each call emits a token metric, tagged with team id. So you can sum token counts per feature.
[00:12:45] Evan: OK. In the pilot we will send a sample of 10k queries across different prompt sizes for benchmarking. Expect that by next Tue.
[00:12:55] Priya: Timeline: if pilot looks good we want to decide by end of Q2 for Dedicated. We may need procurement and legal signoff — what's typical contract lead time?
[00:13:05] Marco: For Dedicated, typical negotiation is 4–6 weeks once SOW and security review are complete; Private deployments can add 2–4 weeks for networking.
[00:13:18] Lena: Will you accept our standard SaaS addendum around data residency?
[00:13:25] Marco: We'll surface that to legal; we've negotiated addenda before.
[00:13:32] Priya: Anything we haven't covered?
[00:13:36] Raj: One last item — observability hooks: can we get per-token breakdown in trace spans? We want to correlate latency spikes with token churn.
[00:13:46] Daniel: Yes; spans include token deltas for request/response phases. We can emit a span for tokenization, model call, and decode. You can attach attributes like team_id and route.
[00:13:58] Priya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[00:14:02] Sofia: Recap — Redwood to send Dedicated pricing + POC template, attach SOC2/KMS docs, share SDK example repo, and schedule a benchmark week of Mar 14. NimbleEdge to share workload samples and compliance list. Action items noted.
[00:14:20] Evan: Sounds good. Any questions before we wrap?
[00:14:24] Lena: None from security besides docs.
[00:14:27] Priya: No, thanks.
[00:14:30] Sofia: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
[00:14:35] (call ends)
